topology: one vLLM replica per node, TP=8 (full node, 8 GCDs)
control: total concurrency scaled with replicas (256 per replica); a fixed-total-concurrency test underestimates scaling
conclusions: Data-parallel scaling is near linear (1.99x at 2 nodes, 3.82x at 4) when concurrency per replica is held constant; parallel efficiency 99.5% and 95.6%.
Cross-node networking adds no measurable per-GCD penalty.
Planning number: ~8.4 rps per GCD at TP=8 => ~30,000 requests per GCD-hour for 7B models.
Throughput per GCD is best at TP=1 (32.0 rps/GCD) and worst at TP=8 (8.8); TP=8 buys latency, not efficiency. DP with TP=1 replicas was not measured, only inferred from the intra-node sweep.
Total-concurrency-fixed tests understate scaling: 2 nodes at conc 256 gives 1.33x because each replica receives half the batch.
